value.rationale: For three independent simultaneous syndrome demands the full 97155-space distribution quantifies how often 3,4,5,6 or 7 accessible coordinates suffice. It refines a known radius seven by showing that only 1200 spaces, about 1.235%, attain the maximum; the remaining distribution matters to average access cost, exact rank-three decoding allocation and testing the boundary of generalized covering-radius estimates. This is a natural complete invariant of the first binary Melas instance of rank-eight syndrome space, not an arbitrary filtered slice.
